report.md:
## This week

You posted 9 videos this week, down from 11 last week. Your views this week landed around 4,100 for a typical video, a bit lower than last week's typical of about 5,300. Your big win was the one that starts with "I launched a company three months ago, and it's already done almost $200,000." That one pulled 605,400 views, way above anything else you posted. Your weakest was the one that starts with "they're going to be. That's totally going to happen." It only got 1,829 views. You also have a brand new one about driving six hours for a passport, but that one only went up yesterday, so it is too early to call it a flop.

## Is it how you film, or what you say?

This is the real question, and right now your videos do not give a clean answer. That is because you tend to film certain topics in certain ways every time, like using talking to camera for almost everything. So it is hard to tell if a video did well because of how you shot it or what you talked about. You have not tested the same script filmed two different ways yet, so that would be your strongest proof, and you do not have that data yet. Right now, what you say seems to matter a little more than how you film it, but nothing here proves that for sure.

## What is working

Your "how you got started" videos usually pull about twice your normal views, and you have posted 24 of them, so that is a real pattern. Your "real money numbers" videos do even better, close to three and a half times normal, across 7 videos. Videos with a link in your bio absolutely crush it, over 16 times your normal views, and you have done this 7 times, so trust it.

## Try this next week

Film one "how you got started" story using voice over footage instead of just talking to camera, since your biggest hit this week used that combo. Take one of your "real money numbers" topics and add a link in your bio call to action, since both boost views on their own. Try filming the exact same script two ways, once talking to camera and once as voice over footage, so you can finally see what really moves the needle.

best.md:
This video did great. You got 16,700 views. That is about four times what a normal video of yours gets.

Your opening line was strong. "This is coming from a girl who made 10k in her first 48 hours, made $100,000 in her first 6 months" stops the scroll and makes people want to know how. That kind of direct value hook does well for you, and this time it did even better than usual.

After that, you kept giving people a reason to stay. You laid out clear steps, one after another, research, build a portfolio, outreach. That step by step structure gives people a reason to keep watching to get the next step.

You did not have a real call to action in the video. The caption mentions a Thursday live, but that is not the same as asking inside the video itself. Next time, ask viewers directly on camera to comment their niche or follow for part two, so you are not relying on the caption to do that work.

One thing to try next time: put a call to action in the middle of the video, right after you give one useful step, not just at the end. That way people who drop off early still see it.

worst.md:
This video did badly. It only got 1,761 views, well under what your videos usually get.

Your opening line was "idk why this always happens to me." It's a relatable moment hook, and that kind of hook usually does okay for you, but here it didn't stop the scroll. There's no speech in the video, just a clip with text, so once the line is read there's nothing pulling people into the next few seconds to find out what "this" even is.

Since there's no voiceover or story building underneath it, the video doesn't give people much reason to stay after that first moment. It's just a clip, so the pull to keep watching fades fast.

There was no call to action on this one. Even something simple like asking people to share a time this happened to them, dropped partway through, could have kept people engaged and gotten you comments.

Next time, pair that same kind of relatable hook with a quick voiceover that explains what's happening, so people have a reason to watch past the first line instead of just reading text on a clip.
